statement.p: Select the trigonometric identity you used in solving this problem.

hint.p: The integral involves \cot u and \csc u where the exponent of \cot u is odd and positive. So we rewrite in order to have a copy of \csc(12 x) \cot(12 x) and use a trigonometric identity to turn the remaining even powers of \cot(12 x) into an expression of \csc^2(12 x). Then use u-substitution with u= \csc(12 x).

Thus the integral can be rewritten as \int 4\cot^{3}\mathopen{}\left(12x\right)\csc^{3}\mathopen{}\left(12x\right) \, dx = 4 \int \cot^2(12 x) \csc^2(12 x) \csc(12 x) \cot(12 x) \, dx = 4 \int \bigg( \csc^2(12 x)-1 \bigg) \csc^2(12 x) \csc(12 x) \cot(12 x) \, dx Now let u= \csc(12 x).
Letting u= \csc(12 x) means that du= -12 \csc(12 x)\cot(12 x) \, dx, and thus dx= \frac{du}{-12\csc(12 x)\cot(12 x)}.
So the integral turns into = 4 \int \bigg( u^2-1 \bigg) u^2 \csc(12 x) \cot(12 x) \frac{du}{-12\csc(12 x)\cot(12 x)}

solution.p: The integral involves \cot u and \csc u where the exponent of \cot u is odd and positive. So we rewrite in order to have a copy of \csc(12 x) \cot(12 x) and use a trigonometric identity to turn the remaining even powers of \cot(12 x) into an expression of \csc^2(12 x).

Then let u= \csc(12 x), which means that du= -12 \csc(12 x)\cot(12 x) \, dx, and thus dx= \frac{du}{-12\csc(12 x)\cot(12 x)}. \begin{aligned} \int 4\cot^{3}\mathopen{}\left(12x\right)\csc^{3}\mathopen{}\left(12x\right) \, dx \amp = 4 \int \cot^2(12 x) \csc^2(12 x) \csc(12 x) \cot(12 x) \, dx \\\\ \amp = 4 \int \bigg( \csc^2(12 x)-1 \bigg) \csc^2(12 x) \csc(12 x) \cot(12 x) \, dx \\\\ \amp = 4 \int \bigg( u^2-1 \bigg) u^2 \csc(12 x) \cot(12 x) \frac{du}{-12\csc(12 x)\cot(12 x)} \\\\ \amp = \frac{4}{-12} \int \bigg( u^2-1 \bigg) u^2 \, du \\\\ \amp = \frac{4}{-12} \int \bigg( u^4-u^2 \bigg) \, du \\\\ \amp = \frac{4}{-12} \bigg[\frac{ u^5}{5}-\frac{u^3}{3}\bigg]+C \\\\ \amp = \frac{4}{-12} \bigg[\frac{ \csc^5(12 x)}{5}-\frac{\csc^3(12 x)}{3}\bigg]+C \end{aligned}
The correct trigonometric identity used is D.
